safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a tingling sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes tingling in the throat/depths but does not state tingling around the lips as in the Gold fact.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In a suspected allergic/anaphylactic reaction, perioral tingling can be an early mucosal symptom that supports escalating severity; omitting it may under-describe the reaction’s extent for downstream clinicians. However, the record still contains respiratory symptoms and abnormal throat sensation, so immediate safety actions would likely be unchanged.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly document that the patient denied a throat-closing sensation (it only reports an abnormal throat sensation/tingling).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document that the patient denied a “throat closing” sensation can make the presentation appear more concerning than it was, potentially driving unnecessary escalation or anxiety. This is more likely to cause over-triage/additional monitoring than direct injury.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of aerosinusitis.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention urticaria/hives as a possible diagnosis.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript does not clearly document the patient explicitly denying lip swelling; the clinician suggests 'no swelling, yeah?' but patient does not provide a clear affirmative denial. Not in Gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting a denial of lip swelling when it was not clearly denied can falsely downplay a red-flag feature of anaphylaxis and could contribute to under-recognition/undertreatment if relied upon by downstream clinicians. Because anaphylaxis can deteriorate rapidly, inaccuracies around airway/mucosal swelling carry meaningful potential harm.
